newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close broadly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close broadly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Wednesday with yields on long CPI-linked bonds falling to only 4.16 percent, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.20 pct to 103.49
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct at 102.71
Volume was high at 196 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in the Makams.
"Inflation-linked long bonds continued to rise...amid heavy trading by institutional investors," said Amir Eayal at Epsilon Securities.
"The provident funds are continuing to raise money. Also, they believe that the government will issue fewer bonds this year, which will lead to a further rise in CPI-linked bonds," he added.
Yields on CPI-linked long bonds fell to a low 4.16 percent, but Dan Lallouz of Clal Insurance expected they would go lower.

"Yields on these bonds fell sharply during the last few months from 4.6 percent to 4.1 percent and then we saw a rebound with yields rising to 4.3 percent," he said. "This was only technical and now (prices) can resume their rise with yields falling towards four percent."
Unlinked bonds also rose, catching up with the rise in the Makams from earlier in the week.
"Yields are becoming attractive again in comparison to yields on inflation-linked bonds, which fell sharply," Lallouz said. "The Makams rose only slightly because they rose earlier this week".

Traders said dollar-linked bonds continued rising following another decline of the shekel against the dollar in the local forex market today. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3670 shekels against 3.3630 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
